sub_indicators.label: Control of state data
sub_indicators.subject: geopol.sovereignty
sub_indicators.text: Digital sovereignty: control of state data
sub_indicators.norm_short: The AU Data Policy Framework asks for localisation of certain categories of data only, with portability so that no one is locked into a single provider; the Digital Transformation Strategy asks for 30 per cent of content hosted in Africa by 2030.
criteria: A source from the past three years says no policy or law governs where state data is held or who may process it.
The government adopted, published or announced a strategy, plan or draft rule to keep government data or systems under national control.
A law, decree or policy in force classifies government data or requires named categories of data to be held in the country.
Government data or a core system is hosted in a government or nationally owned data centre or cloud in the country.
A government contract or agreement with a foreign provider or partner includes terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or handing over source code.
